plan.title: Context Lake: the shared-state layer for multi-agent systems
plan.thesis: Multi-agent systems need a shared, temporal, governed context layer (a 'context lake') distinct from vector stores and per-agent memory.
plan.audience: AI engineers and SRE/platform teams building multi-agent systems in production

questions.question: What is a context lake, who coined the term, and how is it defined?
How does shared context for agents differ from vector databases, data lakes, feature stores and per-agent memory frameworks?
Which systems implement shared or temporal context for agents today, and what do they claim or measure?
What failures in multi-agent systems come from inconsistent or missing shared context, and what is the evidence?
queries: why do multi-agent LLM systems fail

questions.question: What are the criticisms, open problems and adoption signals for context layers in agent systems?

sources.title: PolyKV: A Shared Asymmetrically-Compressed KV Cache Pool for Multi-Agent LLM Inference

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: PolyKV is a system where multiple concurrent inference agents share one asymmetrically compressed KV cache pool.
claims.quote: We present PolyKV, a system in which multiple concurrent inference agents share a single, asymmetrically compressed KV cache pool.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The standard paradigm allocates a separate KV cache per agent, while PolyKV writes a compressed cache once and injects it into N independent agent contexts via HuggingFace DynamicCache objects.
claims.quote: Rather than allocating a separate KV cache per agent -- the standard paradigm -- PolyKV writes a compressed cache once and injects it into N independent agent contexts via HuggingFace DynamicCache objects.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: PolyKV uses asymmetric compression: keys are int8-quantized q8_0 to preserve softmax stability, while values use TurboQuant MSE with FWHT rotation followed by 3-bit Lloyd-Max quantization with centroids tuned to N(0,1).
claims.quote: Compression is asymmetric: Keys are quantized at int8 (q8_0) to preserve softmax stability, while Values are compressed using TurboQuant MSE -- a Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT) rotation followed by 3-bit Lloyd-Max quantization with centroids tuned to N(0,1).

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: PolyKV was evaluated across two model scales, SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B-Instruct, three context lengths from 600 to 7,194 tokens, and up to 15 concurrent agents.
claims.quote: We evaluate across two model scales (SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B-Instruct), three context lengths (600-7,194 tokens), and up to 15 concurrent agents.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: PolyKV reports a stable 2.91x compression ratio across all configurations.
claims.quote: PolyKV achieves a stable 2.91x compression ratio across all configurations.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: On Llama-3-8B with 15 agents sharing a 4K-token context, PolyKV reduces KV cache memory from 19.8 GB to 0.45 GB, a 97.7% reduction, with +0.57% perplexity degradation and mean BERTScore F1 of 0.928.
claims.quote: On Llama-3-8B with 15 agents sharing a 4K-token context, PolyKV reduces KV cache memory from 19.8 GB to 0.45 GB -- a 97.7% reduction -- while maintaining only +0.57% perplexity degradation and a mean BERTScore F1 of 0.928.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: PolyKV reports that PPL delta does not grow with agent count and improves as context length increases, becoming -0.26% at 1,851 coherent tokens.
claims.quote: PPL delta does not grow with agent count and improves as context length increases, inverting to -0.26% at 1,851 coherent tokens.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The authors claim no prior work combines a single shared, lossy-compressed KV pool with multi-reader concurrent agent access.
claims.quote: To our knowledge, no prior work combines a single shared, lossy-compressed KV pool with multi-reader concurrent agent access.

sources.title: FluctlightDB: A Memory Model of Data for AI Agents

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The paper argues relational and vector models were not built for cue-driven, provenance-weighted recall across long sessions, and proposes treating long-term agent memory as a distinct data model with its own write and read semantics.
claims.quote: The relational model asked which records match a predicate; the vector model asked which vectors lie nearest a query. Neither was built for cue-driven, provenance-weighted recall across long sessions. We propose treating long-term agent memory as a distinct data model -- with its own write semantics (encoding, separation, consolidation, provenance) and read semantics (cue-driven activation across a linked memory graph) -- and present FluctlightDB, an embedded engine that implements this contract via experience() and activate().

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The authors say FluctlightDB does not claim novelty over Mem0, Zep, or HippoRAG-style memory layers, positioning it as an embedded engine contract beneath them.
claims.quote: We do not claim novelty over Mem0, Zep, or HippoRAG-style memory layers, only an embedded engine contract beneath them.

claims.question: q3
